title: Being quasi-separated is fpqc local on the base
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that quasi-separatedness is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 5707-5711). The proof records base-change stability and Zariski locality, then reduces to a flat surjective morphism of affines with quasi-separated base change: quasi-separatedness of f' means the diagonal Delta' is quasi-compact, and the proof observes that Delta' is the base change of Delta : X -> X x_S X along S' -> S, so descent of quasi-compactness makes Delta quasi-compact, which is quasi-separatedness of f; the general locality lemma concludes (proof lines 5713-5728). The level is H2: shorter than its separated sibling, but the reduction of the property of f to a property of the diagonal and the identification of that diagonal as a base change are both written out.
